description: Dragon and Dragon compatibility in the Chinese zodiac: the same animal, their Earth elements, yin-yang, and what helps the pairing.
answer: In Chinese astrology, two Dragons share the same branch, Earth element and Yang polarity, so the match is read as a mirror. Each recognises the other's vitality, ambition and confidence; the pairing tends to work best when the shared blind spot, the Dragon's pride, is named early.
ogLine: Two Dragons often form a powerful, ambitious and charismatic partnership with grand shared plans.

sections.heading: How two Dragons relate
paragraphs: The Dragon tends to bring vitality, generosity and big plans to a relationship. It often makes a partner feel part of something exciting. On first meeting, the Dragon often comes across as confident, lively and impressive. Traditional readings associate the Dragon with vitality, ambition and confidence, and in a same-animal pair that quality is present twice. What the Dragon tends to value most in a partner is admiration balanced with honesty, and the strength to stand beside it as an equal. Grand gestures, bold dreams and an appreciative audience tend to keep a Dragon's heart engaged. Magnificent ambitions shared openly rarely fail to captivate it.

Two Dragons may have been born in the same year or twelve, twenty-four or more years apart, so their year elements can differ even though the animal is shared. The Dragon usually needs admiration, honesty and a partner with their own strength and ambitions. Both partners usually need this at once, which can be a source of deep understanding or of competition for the same thing. Friends often notice that two Dragons share habits as well as values, from how they handle plans to how they greet strangers.

sections.heading: What the tradition says about a same-animal pair
paragraphs: When both partners are Dragons, the Chinese zodiac pairs an animal with itself. Classical tables do not list same-animal pairs among the harmonies or clashes; traditional readings instead describe them as mirrors, in which the Dragon's vitality, ambition and confidence is shared and so are its blind spots. Two Dragons often form a powerful, ambitious and charismatic partnership with grand shared plans. Each admires the other's energy. The risk is competing egos and battles for control. Pairs of Dragons tend to do best when they share leadership and direct their ambition outward.

Every Dragon shares the Water trine with the Rat and Monkey, has the Rooster as its Liu He secret friend, and sits opposite the Dog in the six clashes. Because the Dragon pairs with itself here, the Water trine still frames the relationship: both partners share the same natural allies and the same opposite. In the traditional double-hour clock, the Dragon also names the hours from 7 am to 9 am.

sections.heading: Five elements and yin-yang
paragraphs: Two Dragons share Earth as their fixed element. In five-element thinking a shared element is read as mutual recognition, so each Dragon tends to understand the other's instincts, with the caution that the same strengths and excesses are doubled. As Yang animals, two Dragons share the same polarity, outward and active in traditional terms. In five-element terms the Dragon's Earth is associated with stability and nourishment, a quality two Dragons hold in common.

In everyday terms, the shared Earth of the Dragon and the Dragon suggests stability, patience and practical care, with the caution that a steady Dragon and a steady Dragon can become set in their ways. Each birth year also carries its own element from the heavenly stems, so a Metal Dragon and a Water Dragon read slightly differently, and two Dragons born exactly twelve years apart will have year elements one step apart in the cycle. For example, the Dragon year of 2012 was a Water year and the Dragon year of 2024 a Wood year, so two Dragons born in those years differ in flavour.

sections.heading: Friction and what helps two Dragons
paragraphs: Under stress, the Dragon can become proud, domineering or impatient, and may find it hard to admit it was wrong. When both partners respond this way at once, the pattern tends to amplify rather than balance out. After an argument, the Dragon may find it hard to admit fault, and a Dragon who acknowledges its good intentions first makes reconciliation easier.

Between two Dragons, friction often looks like competing visions, each certain of the right course and reluctant to defer. Pride can turn small disagreements into battles. Separating domains of leadership, and praising each other's ideas generously, tends to keep two bright flames from scorching each other.

What helps with a Dragon is honest feedback delivered with respect, shared ambitions and genuine appreciation for its efforts. For two Dragons, agreeing in advance who will step back first when the Dragon's pride appears can keep a shared trait from becoming a shared problem, and taking turns in that role keeps it fair.

sections.heading: Two Dragons day to day
paragraphs: At home, the Dragon tends to think big, planning renovations, celebrations and ambitious projects, and appreciating a Dragon who shares its enthusiasm. Celebrations in a Dragon household tend to be generous, memorable and slightly theatrical. Two Dragons often make an entrance together, with big plans, bold style and plenty of mutual admiration. Leadership can become a tug of war, so deciding who directs which ventures lets two magnificent egos cheer each other on rather than collide.

Traditionally the Dragon usually enjoys grand, exciting outings such as festivals, luxury trips, performances and ambitious shared projects, which two Dragons can enjoy side by side. As a colleague, the Dragon inspires and drives ambitious goals; beside the Dragon, it brings vision and the confidence to pursue it. Pitches, transformations and ambitious launches are where the Dragon's energy is often most useful. On a shared team, two Dragons tend to reinforce each other's vitality, which is a real asset once roles are clearly divided.

faq.question: Are the Dragon and the Dragon compatible in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Classical tables do not rate same-animal pairs as harmonies or clashes. Two Dragons tend to understand each other quickly and share the same blind spot, the Dragon's pride, so awareness matters more than any rating.

faq.question: What are the elements of the Dragon?
faq.answer: The Dragon's fixed element is Earth and its polarity is Yang. Each birth year adds a separate year element from the heavenly stems.

faq.question: Which animals are best for the Dragon?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rat and Monkey share the Dragon's San He trine and the Rooster is its Liu He secret friend.

faq.question: What might the Dragon and the Dragon enjoy doing together?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Dragon usually enjoys grand, exciting outings such as festivals, luxury trips, performances and ambitious shared projects. Two Dragons often enjoy these side by side, and taking turns to choose keeps plans fresh.

faq.question: Does the Chinese zodiac use the calendar year?
faq.answer: No. Animal years begin at Lunar New Year: the Dragon year of 2024 began on February 10, and the one before it, in 2012, on January 23, so January birthdays need checking. The calculator does this automatically.
